newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai ARY gold trader halts business to Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Dubai ARY gold trader halts business to Pakistan.

text.p: Dubai-based ARY Traders, the sole importers of gold and silver into Pakistan, have not made any shipments in the past two weeks amid concern in Pakistan of the validity of their import licence, a company official said.

"Media reports in Pakistan raised speculation about our licence being revoked, but we have received assurances from the government that our licence is still valid," Abdul Razzak, ARY's chief executive and managing director, told Reuters.
"Local banks through whom we sell our gold and silver as stipulated in our licence are sceptical, they want clearance in the form of written assurances," he said.
Razzak said ARY had approached Pakistan's commerce ministry for written confirmation of the legality of their licence, but the document, promised 10 days ago, had not been received.
"We keep getting promises that the letter will be issued, but nothing has happened so far," Razzak said.
He said gold prices in Pakistan had shot up since the suspension of ARY imports there due to short supplies.
ARY traders were awarded the import licence in early 1995.

Khaleej Times quoted Razzak as saying said newspapers had carried reports that the caretaker government had awarded similar licences to two firms in Karachi and Lahore, but no official announcement had been made.
Dubai is a major gold trading centre.
